note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: CORRECTION (Oct 21): no US shutdown — Trump signed the CR Sept 2, funded through Dec 11; Sept jobs/CPI/PPI/housing all printed on schedule (the 'shutdown day 20' line was bad data). 20-yr auction (Oct 21): $13B at 5.469% — record since the May-2020 reintroduction; tailed WI by 0.9bp (4th tail); B/C 2.73; indirects 58.2% (avg 65.2% — soft foreign demand) — 'softer-than-expected' (Dow Jones/WSJ), little market reaction. France: revenue-section vote postponed (first reading to Oct 27; FinMin Lescure floated Article 49.3); OAT 4.948% (+2.9bp, WSJ/Tradeweb); OAT-Bund ~153bp; Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 neg, cut to A1 expected). UK: Sep borrowing £24.5B miss (vs £23.9B); debt >£3T; Healey Budget Oct 28.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: US: housing soft patch (starts 1.221M miss, pending home sales -7.3% record low, ADP 18.5K) vs last week's retail/IP beats — net mixed; jobless claims print 7:30 CT (200K fcst, 199K prev). UK: jobs beat (unemp 4.7%) + GDP +0.1% beat vs CBI orders -32 miss. China: Q3 GDP 4.5% beat; FDI decline narrowing (-4.3% y/y Jan-Sep). Australia: employment -39.3K, unemp 4.7% five-year high.
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: UK Sep CPI verified 3.5% y/y beat (vs 3.4% fcst; highest since Oct 2025 on energy; core 2.8% in line; services 3.7% sticky; PPI +4.6% vs 4.3%) — reinforces the priced Nov-5 BoE path, no repricing. German Sep PPI +6.7% y/y beat (vs 6.2%). US CPI 3.7%, PPI hot; import prices +8.1% y/y. NZ Q3 CPI printed 0.7% q/q, 3.7% y/y — soft miss vs 0.8%/3.8% fcst (below RBNZ 3.9% proj, still above 1–3% target). Japan national core CPI tonight 18:30 CT (2.1% fcst, prev 1.7%).
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: FOMC Oct 27-28: hold ~84-85% (FedWatch, Oct 21; ~16% hike odds) — blackout, no speakers; December hike ~90%. BoC Oct-28 hike ~93% (CORRA OIS); RBNZ Oct-28 hike ~98% (Reuters, Oct 22; 100% chance of 50bp by end-Feb) after the soft Q3 CPI. ECB Oct 29: hold virtually certain (70/73 economists); Dec hike ~76% (current vintage); IMF expects ≥1 more 25bp hike in 2026. BoE Nov 5: ~98.8% (LSEG); Dec back-to-back ~51%. RBA Nov 2-3: ~42% (Goldman flipped to a Nov call). BoJ Oct 29-30: hold ~88-90%; Dec ~80% (ex-BoJ Maeda via Japan Times/Bloomberg).
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). Crowded trades are fragile: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: New CFTC (Oct 13 report): all G10 signals neutral (0). Splits: hedge funds flipped AGAINST the yen while real money bets FOR it; hedge funds for the Aussie but real money strongly against. Funds strongly short CAD (added sharply). No crowded-long unwind risk anywhere — the pain trade is two-sided.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: DXY extends slide as US yields stretch lower (FXStreet) into the 7:30 CT claims print — no real dollar haven bid even on the Gulf escalation. Yen's best day in a month: USD/JPY broke below 157.5 (Asia low 157.4), lowest since early October, on dollar-long paring + risk-off; Asian stocks hit a 3-month low. Iran claims seven Gulf ships hit (unverified); US ordered embassy staff/families out of Saudi Arabia (Oct 21). France protests continue.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Brent back above $110.75 on fresh Gulf shipping hits (Reuters, Oct 22); WTI ~$99. EIA: crude -3.1M bbl draw (10x expected). Eurozone natural gas >EUR 90/MWh (first since Dec 2022). Gold ~$4,115 — 5th down day, trading Dec-hike odds (~90%) not oil headlines.
tot.title: Terms of trade
